references.text: The same chapter describes that whoever carries any of these dead animals shall be unclean until evening and must wash their clothes.
Further instructions in the same chapter regarding uncleanness from dead animals and the necessity of washing clothes and remaining unclean until evening.
Rules state that clay vessels touched by an unclean person must be broken, while wooden vessels must be rinsed with water.
Open vessels without lids become unclean when they come into contact with uncleanness.
Purification of clothes, leather items, goat hair products, and wooden objects after war.
Purification with water on the seventh day for objects that cannot withstand fire.
Clay pots in which a sin offering was cooked must be broken, while bronze pots must be scrubbed and rinsed with water.
Whoever enters a house with leprosy is unclean until evening, and whoever lies down or eats there must wash their clothes.
A priest who is unclean shall remain unclean until evening and must not eat of the holy offerings until he has bathed in water.
